subject: Conditional regional fallback window: request for RTO/RPO exception
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@acmepay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+compliance@acmepay.com
Date: 2029-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Conditional fallback window: RTO/RPO carveout request

Vanessa —

Thanks for the call yesterday. As discussed with our compliance and SRE teams, AcmePay needs a short formal request outlining any proposed deviations from Redwood's standard multi-region SLA for EU => US failover. The specific asks we need documented are:

- Maximum RTO for cross-region failover (EU primary to US warm-standby).
- Maximum RPO / replication lag allowed during the exception window.
- Any compensating controls (read-only periods, geo-fencing, telemetry).
- Activation lead time and test cadence.

We also need copies of: a high-level DR runbook, the SOC 2 Type II summary, and an estimate of additional reserved capacity required to guarantee a sub-15m RTO if you think that's feasible.

Can you provide a proposed exception (duration, limits) and the evidence items by next week? Acme's legal and security teams will need to review before we can sign any amendment.

— Rajiv
Rajiv Menon
Head of Platform Security, AcmePay
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@acmepay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Conditional fallback window: RTO/RPO carveout request

Rajiv —

Thanks for outlining the requirements. Below is a preliminary proposal from Redwood for a time-bound exception that balances your compliance needs with operational realities of cross-region failover. This is intended as a starting point; we'll formalize in an amendment once we agree on controls and pricing.

Proposed exception (EU primary → US warm-standby):
- Exception window: ongoing, with quarterly review; capacity and controls revalidated each quarter.
- Cross-region RTO: 60 minutes (activation + full traffic cutover).
- Cross-region RPO: up to 1 hour replication lag for non-critical writes. Critical ledgers must remain pinned to EU (see compensating controls).
- Activation lead time: 30 minutes notice recommended for planned switchovers; automatic failover escalation for active incidents.

Compensating controls we propose to include in the amendment:
- Read-only redirect for a configurable subset of write-heavy routes during failover.
- Per-route prioritization and a warmed replica pool for your highest-throughput models.
- Enhanced telemetry (replication lag, KV hit/miss, token-level latency) surfaced to a shared dashboard for the exception window.
- Quarterly DR tests with pre-announced and unannounced windows.

Attachments provided with this email: redwood-drs-runbook.pdf (high-level steps), soc2-type-ii-summary.pdf. We'll follow up with a capacity estimate (capacity-estimate.csv) and a draft SLA amendment (amendment-draft.pdf).

Notes / caveats:
- For read/write heavy workloads that require under-5m RTO/RPO, we recommend reserving dedicated capacity in both regions (additional cost).
- Some model state (large KV caches, warmed GPU kernels) will incur a cold-start cost if not pre-warmed; that impacts median failover latency. Karthik & Markus, I tagged you for the technical and pricing implications below.

Next steps:
1) I'll circulate a formal amendment draft (amendment-draft.pdf) by Monday.
2) Karthik/Markus to provide a capacity estimate and options for a pre-warmed lane.
3) Rajiv: confirm whether AcmePay accepts the 60m/1h proposed limits as a baseline for legal review.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@acmepay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+compliance@acmepay.com
Date: 2029-08-23T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Conditional fallback window: RTO/RPO carveout request

Vanessa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying questions before we escalate to legal:

1) The 1 hour RPO is larger than AcmePay's usual tolerance. Can Redwood commit to a maximum documented replication lag for the warmed-replica configuration (e.g., 90s avg, 5m peak) if we accept the 60m RTO?
2) For the read-only redirect: can that be scoped per route and enacted automatically as part of the runbook? We need automated, auditable steps rather than manual cutovers.

If you can show a path to sub-5m replication lag for a defined critical subset of endpoints (with cost estimate), we may accept broader RPO on non-critical endpoints.

— Rajiv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rajiv Menon <r.menon@acmepay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-08-24T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Conditional fallback window: RTO/RPO carveout request

Rajiv / Vanessa —

Technical context on the 60m / 1h proposal and options for tighter bounds: 

- Warmed replica behavior: Our warm-standby model keeps model weights loaded, but KV caches and per-session context still need warming. With a pre-warmed lane (dedicated GPUs in the standby region with ongoing lightweight traffic), we can target replication lag ≤ 90s for the critical subset and median cutover times under 10 minutes for those routes.

- Trade-offs: To reach ≤ 90s replication lag consistently we recommend:
  * Dedicated standby slice for critical routes (pre-warmed GPUs).
  * Incremental cross-region replication for critical state (near real-time changefeed).
  * SLA-backed priority routing during activation.

- Cost impact: Dedicated standby and near-RT replication adds a predictable monthly reservation (~estimated in capacity-estimate.csv attached). If Acme wants an on-demand fallback to sub-5m RTO/RPO across all routes that's materially higher (full active-active replication).

I'll attach conservative and aggressive capacity estimates. If Acme confirms which routes are critical, we can model a mixed approach (critical routes: ≤ 90s replication, non-critical: up to 1h).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-08-28T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Conditional fallback window: RTO/RPO carveout request — proposed amendment and next steps

Rajiv —

Following internal follow-ups, please find the agreed proposal and next steps below. This consolidates our prior messages and Karthik's technical options into an amendment draft.

Agreed baseline for amendment:
- Scoped exception (EU primary -> US standby): 60m RTO for non-critical routes, 1h RPO for non-critical routes.
- Critical route carveout: Dedicated pre-warmed standby slice with target replication lag <= 90s and target RTO <= 10m. Critical routes must be designated by Acme in writing.
- Activation: automated runbook steps for read-only redirect + priority routing; runbook excerpt included in amendment-draft.pdf.
- Testing: quarterly DR tests (one unannounced per year).
- Price: capacity estimates and options are in capacity-estimate.csv; we'll propose a monthly reservation for the critical-slice option.

We have attached: amendment-draft.pdf (formal language), redwood-drs-runbook.pdf, soc2-type-ii-summary.pdf, capacity-estimate.csv.

If this looks acceptable, please:
1) Confirm the list of critical routes by 2029-09-04.
2) Legal can sign the amendment via the DocuSign link here: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/ACM-DR-AMEND-2029.

If Acme would like to push for a hard universal sub-5m RTO/RPO across all routes, we can provide a separate active-active proposal and pricing, but that will be a different amendment.

Thanks — we can hop on a 30m call if you want to walk through the amendment.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
